types.embedding_query_text: Commodity: A raw material or primary product that can be bought or sold. Also called Resource, Material, Good. Examples: Oil, Gas, LNG, Brent crude.

chosen_type.label: Product
chosen_type.justification: Best fit for commodity mentions like 'Oil', 'Gas', 'LNG'

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: Store
candidates.comment: A retail business that sells goods to consumers. Also called shop, retail outlet, boutique, market. Examples: a grocery store, a clothing store, an electronics store, a bookstore.

types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation with its own government, occupying a defined territory. Also called Nation, State, Republic. Examples: US, Iran, Yemen, Saudi Arabia.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: Direct match for country mentions like 'US', 'Iran', 'Yemen', 'Saudi Arabia'

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: SingleFamilyResidence
candidates.comment: A type of house designed to be occupied by one family, typically detached from other homes. Also called detached house, single-family home, private residence. Examples: a suburban house with a yard, a standalone cottage, a bungalow.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

types.embedding_query_text: ShippingRoute: A path or course used for transporting goods or people by sea. Also called TradeRoute, NavigationChannel, MaritimeRoute. Examples: Strait of Hormuz.

chosen_type.label: ShippingRoute
chosen_type.definition: A path or course used for transporting goods or people by sea.
chosen_type.justification: No direct match in schema.org for shipping routes like 'Strait of Hormuz'

candidates.label: BoatTrip
candidates.comment: A Trip representing a journey taken on a commercial ferry line or similar water transport. Also called ferry journey, boat excursion, water travel. Examples: "A ferry trip across the English Channel", "A sightseeing boat trip on the river", "A commercial fishing boat trip". Distinct from BoatReservation, which is the booking for the trip.

candidates.label: TrainTrip
candidates.comment: A journey or itinerary undertaken using a commercial train line. Also called rail journey, train travel, railway trip. Examples: a cross-country train journey, a daily commute by train, a scenic train ride through the mountains.

candidates.label: ShippingService
candidates.comment: A structured value defining the criteria used to determine if and how an offer can be shipped to a customer. Also called delivery option, shipping method, freight service, courier choice. Examples: 'Standard Ground Shipping', 'Expedited Air Delivery', 'International Economy Shipping'.

candidates.label: ShippingRateSettings
candidates.comment: A structured value representing reusable shipping rate information, often linked to an offer via a shipping settings link. Also called shipping cost rules, freight pricing, delivery charges configuration. Examples: a flat rate shipping setting for standard delivery, a weight-based shipping rate table, a zone-based shipping cost.

candidates.label: Canal
candidates.comment: An artificial waterway constructed for navigation, irrigation, or drainage. Also called waterway, artificial channel, navigation channel. Examples: Panama Canal, Suez Canal, Erie Canal, Grand Canal of China.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: A human being, especially an adult. Also called Individual, Human, Man. Examples: Susannah Streeter, Massimo Di Odoardo.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Best fit for person mentions like 'Susannah Streeter', 'Massimo Di Odoardo'

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A group of people working together for a common purpose. Also called Company, Institution, Association. Examples: Wealth Club.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: Direct match for organization mentions like 'Wealth Club'

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: Cooperative
candidates.comment: A Cooperative is an organization formed as a joint project by multiple organizations or individuals, often for mutual benefit. Also called member-owned business, co-op, collective. Examples: REI (Recreational Equipment, Inc.), Ocean Spray, Sunkist Growers, credit unions. Distinct from Corporation, which is a business entity owned by shareholders.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

types.embedding_query_text: ResearchGroup: A team of people conducting research and analysis. Also called ThinkTank, Institute, Laboratory. Examples: Wood McKenzie.

chosen_type.label: ResearchOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Best fit for research group mentions like 'Wood McKenzie'

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: ResearchProject
candidates.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

candidates.label: Researcher
candidates.comment: A Researcher is an Audience type representing individuals engaged in scientific or academic inquiry. Also called scientist, academic, scholar. Examples: a university professor, a lab scientist, a PhD student, an independent scholar.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

types.embedding_query_text: CentralBank: A national bank that manages a country's currency and monetary policy. Also called ReserveBank, MonetaryAuthority, FinancialInstitution. Examples: European Central Bank, Bank of England, ECB, BoE.

chosen_type.label: BankOrCreditUnion
chosen_type.justification: Closest match for central bank mentions like 'European Central Bank', 'Bank of England'

candidates.label: BankOrCreditUnion
candidates.comment: A FinancialService provided by an institution that handles money and credit for customers. Also called bank, credit union, financial institution. Examples: "Chase Bank", "Navy Federal Credit Union", "Citibank". Distinct from AutomatedTeller, which is a machine, not an institution.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: CurrencyConversionService
candidates.comment: A CurrencyConversionService is a financial service that facilitates the exchange of funds from one currency to another. Also called foreign exchange service, money exchange, currency exchange. Examples: A bank's foreign exchange desk, an online currency converter, a travel money service.

candidates.label: BankAccount
candidates.comment: A FinancialProduct or service offered by a bank for depositing, withdrawing, or transferring money, often with interest. Also called bank account, checking account, savings account, deposit account. Examples: "My personal checking account", "A business savings account", "A joint current account".

candidates.label: FinancialService
candidates.comment: A FinancialService is a LocalBusiness that provides financial services. Also called bank, credit union, investment firm, insurance company. Examples: A retail bank, a wealth management firm, an insurance agency, a loan provider.

types.embedding_query_text: MilitantGroup: A group of people using violence to achieve their goals. Also called RebelGroup, InsurgentGroup, TerroristOrganization. Examples: Houthi militia.

chosen_type.label: MilitantGroup
chosen_type.definition: An organization that uses violence to achieve its goals.
chosen_type.justification: No direct match in schema.org for militant groups like 'Houthi militia'

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

candidates.label: DanceGroup
candidates.comment: A DanceGroup is a performing organization specializing in dance, often presenting choreographed performances. Also called dance company, ballet troupe, dance ensemble, dance collective. Examples: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Riverdance, New York City Ballet, Bolshoi Ballet.

types.embedding_query_text: BodyOfWater: A large area of water, such as an ocean, sea, or lake. Also called Ocean, Sea, Lake. Examples: Red Sea.

chosen_type.label: BodyOfWater
chosen_type.justification: Direct match for body of water mentions like 'Red Sea'

candidates.label: BodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A Landform representing a significant accumulation of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake. Also called aquatic environment, water body, large water mass. Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

candidates.label: SeaBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A large expanse of saltwater, typically part of an ocean or a large inland body of saltwater. Also called sea, ocean, marine body, saltwater expanse. Examples: the Mediterranean Sea, the Caribbean Sea, the Black Sea, the Caspian Sea. Distinct from RiverBodyOfWater, which is a flowing freshwater course.

candidates.label: OceanBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: An OceanBodyOfWater, as a BodyOfWater, is a large expanse of saltwater, such as the Pacific Ocean. Also called ocean, sea, marine body. Examples: Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, Southern Ocean. Distinct from LakeBodyOfWater, which is an inland freshwater body.

candidates.label: LakeBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A LakeBodyOfWater is a landform representing a large body of still water surrounded by land. Also called lake, inland sea, reservoir. Examples: Lake Superior, Lake Tahoe, Lake Pontchartrain. Distinct from River, which is flowing water, and OceanBodyOfWater, which is a large saltwater body.

candidates.label: RiverBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A natural flowing watercourse, typically freshwater, flowing towards an ocean, sea, lake, or another river. Also called river, stream, waterway, current. Examples: the Nile River, the Amazon River, the Mississippi River, the Thames. Distinct from SeaBodyOfWater, which is a large expanse of saltwater.

types.embedding_query_text: Month: A period of time, typically 30 or 31 days, used to divide the year. Also called Period, Timeframe, Season. Examples: June.

chosen_type.label: Month
chosen_type.definition: A unit of time, equal to one twelfth of a year.
chosen_type.justification: Not a perfect match but closest for month mentions like 'June'

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

types.embedding_query_text: TimePeriod: A specific duration of time, such as a week or a year. Also called Duration, Interval, Span. Examples: Last week.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: Best fit for time period mentions like 'Last week'

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

types.embedding_query_text: Year: A period of 365 or 366 days, used to measure time. Also called Period, Timeframe, Cycle. Examples: 2027.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: Best fit for year mentions like '2027'

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

chosen_type.justification: Best fit for storage facility mentions like 'European gas storage'

candidates.label: EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration listing the EU energy efficiency classes A-G, A+, A++, and A+++ as defined in EU directive 2017/1369. Also called EU energy rating, European energy class. Examples: EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA, EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA+++, EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryG.

candidates.label: GasStation
candidates.comment: A GasStation is an AutomotiveBusiness that sells fuel for vehicles. Also called petrol station, filling station, service station. Examples: Shell, ExxonMobil, a local independent gas station.

candidates.label: SelfStorage
candidates.comment: A local business providing rental units for individuals and businesses to store their belongings. Also called storage facility, mini-storage, public storage. Examples: 'U-Haul Self-Storage', 'Extra Space Storage', 'Local Storage Units'.

candidates.label: ParkingFacility
candidates.comment: A ParkingFacility is a civic structure providing space for parking vehicles. Also called parking lot, parking garage, car park. Examples: a multi-story parking garage, a supermarket parking lot, a valet parking service. Distinct from Road, which is for vehicle travel.

candidates.label: EnergyConsumptionDetails
candidates.comment: EnergyConsumptionDetails is an Intangible providing information related to the energy efficiency of a product that consumes energy, based on international regulations. Also called energy efficiency data, power usage specifications, consumption metrics. Examples: A product's energy label showing kWh/year, details on standby power consumption, information on energy efficiency class.
